evidence: comment references to 'Open Cobol v3.00.00' and 'GC 3.2'

purpose.summary: Invoice Data Entry and Maintenance program for the Applewood Computers Accounting System (ACAS). Handles both batch and immediate invoice printing, credit notes, stock updates, and audit trail writing. Calls multiple sub-modules for stock, sales, delivery, analysis, and open-item file processing.

notable_features: 19 CALL statements to external sub-modules (acas010–acas019, sl070, sl930, sl960, etc.)
107 PERFORM and 107 GOTO statements indicating complex procedural flow
COPY statements for environment, FD, and WS sections (copybook-heavy architecture)
Support for VAT codes (Standard/Reduced/Zero), credit notes, pro-formas
RDB/FH (FileHandler/DAL) migration noted in comments from v3.02 onward
Screen-based data entry with function key handling (F1, F2, etc.)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
verdict.notes: This is clearly a long-lived production COBOL program (1976–2023) for a sales ledger/invoice entry system. The >>source free directive and *> comments confirm GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL). All four COBOL divisions are present. The file uses extensive copybooks (all commented out in the visible section, replaced by inline WS definitions), suggesting a modular architecture. The truncation at 16000 chars covers roughly the first 18% of the file; the remainder likely contains the PROCEDURE DIVISION with the bulk of the logic.
